<style>
/* 1. Global Page Background */
body {
  background-color: #FAEDEA; 
}

/* 2. Generalized Background for ALL Output blocks */
pre {
  background-color: #ffffff; /* White background for Output */
  border-radius: 4px;
  padding: 1px;
}

/* 3. Different Background JUST for Source Code blocks */
/* This overrides the above rule only if it is actually code */
pre:has(code[class*="language-"]) {
  background-color: #C5C6F1; /* light purple */
  color: black;            /* Light text for Code */
}

/* Optional: Keep your inline code slightly different to stand out in text */
code {
  background-color: #e8e8e8; 
  padding: 2px 4px;
  border-radius: 3px;
}
</style>

# Introduction
Your code will now be dark, and the outputs will be white. And because we didn't use hyper-specific overrides, it's natively much cleaner!



```r
print("This code and the output underneath will now share the same simple style!")
```

`r`

```{r, echo = T}
x <- data.table(a=1:10, b=letters[1:10])
tinytable::tt(x)
```
